**STEP 1 - Scene:** A hospital-style tray meal photographed from the front at a slightly elevated angle. It has a main dish of meat in brown gravy, a bowl of cooked mixed vegetables, and a glass of water. A colour calibration card sits at the lower left.

**STEP 2 - Ruler:** The main plate is an oval, about 22 cm long and 17 cm wide, so its area is about 294 cm². The vegetable bowl is about 15 cm across, so its area is about 177 cm². Neither is a standard size, so these are estimates.

**STEP 3 - Items:** (a) meat pieces in brown gravy, (b) carrot slices, (c) sweet corn kernels, (d) broccoli florets.

**STEP 4 - Area:** The gravy-covered meat covers about 75% of the main plate (about 220 cm²). The vegetables cover about 50% of the bowl (about 88 cm²), made up of roughly 25% carrot, 15% corn and 10% broccoli.

**STEP 5 - Volume:** The meat and gravy mound is about 2 cm high, giving about 440 ml. The vegetable pile is about 2 cm high on about 88 cm², giving about 177 ml, split into carrot (~70 ml), corn (~50 ml) and broccoli (~30 ml).

**STEP 6 - Grams:** Meat in gravy at 0.7 g/ml (gravy and gaps reduce the dense-meat figure) gives about 310 g; in practice I use 300 g. Cut vegetables at 0.5–0.6 g/ml give carrot ~40 g, corn ~30 g and broccoli ~10 g.

**STEP 7 - Energy:** Meat in gravy at about 120 kcal/100 g gives about 360 kcal. Carrot at 35 kcal/100 g gives about 14 kcal. Sweet corn at 90 kcal/100 g gives about 27 kcal. Broccoli at 34 kcal/100 g gives about 3 kcal.

**STEP 8 - Sanity check:** A main plate about three-quarters full of meat in gravy plus a half-full small vegetable bowl is plausible at roughly 380 g and about 400 kcal in total. The water is not counted.
